segments.he: מְאד, וּפַעַם אַחַת דִּבֵּר הַרְבֵּה מֵעִנְיַן זֶה שֶּׁנּוֹהֲגִין הָעוֹלָם לְהַעֲשִׁין טִיטוּן וְאָמַר שֶׁהוּא שְׁטוּת גָּדוֹל, וּלְעִנְיַן נְקִיּוּת אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל כְּלָל. וְכֵן הָרֵיחַ טַבַּק שֶׁהוּא גָּרוּעַ עוֹד יוֹתֵר, כַּמְבאָר שִׂיחָה זאת בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר:
segments.en: (2.) I heard in his name that he said he dreamed a witticism — and it is this one [Shabbos 34a]: "Harlots adorn each other — Torah scholars kal vachomer [all the more so]." The difficulty is: harlots adorn each other — Torah scholars "not?" Meaning: since harlots adorn each other, why do Torah scholars not honor each other? And the answer is kal vachomer — meaning for the sake of kal vachomer — for the sake of money, which is called kal vachomer, for kal vachomer is wealth...
